newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - GTE on long distance and MCI.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - GTE on long distance and MCI.

text.p: GTE Corp on Wednesday said it expected to have its millionth long distance customer at the start of March and is on target for 1.5 million by the end of 1997.
"We're on target so far this year," Charles Lee, GTE Chief Executive and Chairman, told Reuters. "We are expecting our millionth long distance customer early next month," Lee said.
GTE began offering long distance services in March 1996 and ended the year with 825,000 customers and it serves the majority of states in the country.

Lee said that this opportunity was very great compared to the regional Bells which must first pass a competitive check list before they are allowed to offer long distance services to their local calling customers.
Lee said that where GTE offers services, it would offer a bundle of services combining local and long distance, Internet access and wireless.
Lee said that GTE was in the process of spending up to $200 million on a software sytem to support the provision of bundled services.
Lee acknowledged that GTE had serious talks about buying MCI Communications Corp last year.
"We talked seriously about getting together," Lee said.
He would not charecterize the talks as breaking down on price grounds.
"It was more general then that," Lee said after giving a speech at an investment conference.
"MCI then decided themselves to go in the dirction of BT," Lee said.
MCI agreed to merge with British Telecommunications Plc late last year in a deal to form a company called Concert Plc. BT already had a 20 percent stake in MCI.
